guest.name: Rahul Deshmukh
guest.title: Mr.
guest.note: fictional; same person as in the Manual System training. Business date 24 Oct 2026 (fixture); demo hotel 24 rooms 101-308.

chapters.title: Welcome: Modules Home and the Dashboard
chapters.goal: Find your way around HCC: the Modules Home tiles, the top bar, search, the menu, Appearance & display and the Dashboard.

steps.say: This is Modules Home, the first screen after you choose your name. Each tile is one module; the red number on a tile is the work waiting there.
steps.why: Everything in HCC starts from these tiles, and you only see the modules your role may use.
steps.expect: Nine module tiles for Reception: Front Desk, Cash & Billing, Housekeeping & Maintenance, Guests & Services, Customers, Revenue & Sales, People & Payroll, Accounts & Reports, Admin & Setup.

steps.say: Look at the top bar. It shows the business date, whether the day is Open, the hotel clock, and who is signed in: Aarav, Reception.
steps.why: Every entry you make carries this business date and your name, so check them before you start work.
steps.expect: Business date 24 Oct 2026, Open, 08:00 IST, Aarav · Reception.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile to open that module.
steps.why: A module page lists its screens as tiles; the number on the tile shows open work.
steps.expect: The Front Desk page opens with tiles such as Room board, Calendar, Reservations, Guests, Arrivals & check-in and Room keys.

steps.say: Look at the breadcrumb at the top left, Modules Home then Front Desk. Click Modules Home to go back.
steps.why: The breadcrumb always shows where you are, and every earlier part of it is a link.
steps.expect: You are back on Modules Home.

steps.say: Press Control and K, or click the Search button in the top bar, to open the search box.
steps.why: Search is the quickest way to any screen, and it also offers quick actions: New reservation, Walk-in guest and Add expense.
steps.expect: The search box opens with the three quick actions and the popular pages.

steps.say: Type part of a name, for example rates. The list narrows as you type.
steps.why: You only see pages your role may open, so a search never leads to a screen you cannot use.
steps.expect: Pages and actions that match the word.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the search box without choosing anything.
steps.why: Escape closes any dialog in HCC and leaves your work as it was.

steps.say: Click the menu button at the top left to open the side menu.
steps.why: The side menu lists every module and page in the same order as the tiles, and has Change my PIN and Sign out.
steps.expect: The side menu opens with Modules Home, the module list, Demo & display, Change my PIN and Sign out.

steps.say: Close the menu, then open Admin & Setup, Appearance & display. Here each person sets text size, theme and start page for this device.
steps.why: These choices belong to this device only. They are not hotel data and they are not audited.
steps.expect: The Appearance & display page opens: text size, theme, density, motion, start page, list size and message time.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, also sees a Dashboard tile that Reception does not have. Click Dashboard to see the day at a glance.
steps.why: The Dashboard gives the manager the day's occupancy, arrivals, cash and open work on one screen.
steps.expect: The Dashboard page opens for Meera (Manager).

chapters.title: Reservations and the Calendar
chapters.goal: Take a booking for Mr. Rahul Deshmukh, hold a room for an enquiry, book a company guest, read the Calendar and cancel a booking.

steps.say: You are Aarav at Reception, on Modules Home. This chapter takes bookings, so you will work in the Front Desk module.
steps.why: Choose the module first, then the screen.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile.
steps.why: Reservations, the Calendar, check-in and the room board all live in this module.

steps.say: Click the Reservations tile.
steps.why: This list holds every booking, past and future.
steps.expect: The Reservations page opens with all bookings.

steps.say: Read the list. Each row shows the guest, booking number, room, stay dates, status, advance paid and folio balance.
steps.why: Reception checks this list before telling a caller whether a booking exists.
steps.expect: The list of all bookings, newest first.

steps.say: Click the Held chip to see only bookings that are on hold.
steps.why: A hold keeps a room for a short time while the guest decides. Held, Expired, Confirmed, In house, Departed, Cancelled and No show each have a chip.

steps.say: Click All, then type a guest name in the search box. Type Ghate.
steps.why: Search finds a booking by guest name, phone number, room number or booking number.
steps.expect: Only bookings of guests named Ghate are listed.

steps.say: Clear the search box to see all bookings again.
steps.why: An old search left in the box hides bookings and confuses the next person.

steps.say: Click New reservation to take a booking.
steps.why: A reservation reserves a room before the guest arrives.

steps.say: The dialog opens with Arrival 24 Oct 2026 and Departure 26 Oct 2026. Rahul Deshmukh stays two nights, so leave the dates as they are.
steps.why: The dates decide the room rate, the tax and the availability list below.

steps.say: Choose 2 adults. Rahul travels with Mrs. Sneha Deshmukh.
steps.why: The number of guests limits which room types can be booked.

steps.say: Choose the room type Deluxe.
steps.why: The list of rooms below shows only the rooms that are free for these dates.
steps.expect: Only free Deluxe rooms are listed.

steps.say: Choose room 203, Deluxe, Rs 3,000 a night.
steps.why: Auto-assign would pick the first free room. Rahul asked for 203, so choose it yourself.

steps.say: Type the guest name: Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: The name on the booking is printed on the registration card and the invoice.

steps.say: Type the mobile number. The training uses a dummy number.
steps.why: The phone number is how reception reaches the guest and finds the booking again.

steps.say: Choose the booking source Phone, because Rahul booked by calling the hotel.
steps.why: The source feeds the reports on where bookings come from.

steps.say: Type the notes: wake-up call at 06:30 on 25 October and two extra towels.
steps.why: Notes travel with the booking so the night staff and housekeeping can see the guest's requests.
steps.value: Wake-up call 06:30 on 25 Oct. Two extra towels.
auto: type:field:Notes|Wake-up call 06:30 on 25 Oct. Two extra towels.

steps.say: Click Confirm reservation.
steps.why: Confirm keeps the room for the guest. Use Hold 2 hours instead when the guest has not decided yet.
steps.expect: The reservation is confirmed as HCC-1101 and its booking dialog opens.
steps.msgText: Reservation confirmed. Open it to register the guest and check in.

steps.say: The booking dialog opens for HCC-1101: Rahul Deshmukh, room 203, 24 to 26 October, Confirmed. The buttons are the actions you can take from here.
steps.why: From this dialog reception changes, cancels, prints and checks in the booking.
steps.expect: The booking dialog with the folio and the action buttons.

steps.say: Click Change dates / room to see how a booking is amended.
steps.why: Guests change plans; the booking can be moved without cancelling it.
steps.expect: The Move / change dates view opens inside the dialog.

steps.say: Change nothing. Click Back.
steps.why: Back returns to the booking without saving anything.
steps.expect: The booking dialog is shown again.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the booking dialog.
steps.why: Escape closes any dialog and leaves the data as it was.

steps.say: Now an enquiry: Mrs. Meena Kulkarni phones but has not decided. Click New reservation.
steps.why: A hold stops another guest taking the room while she decides.
steps.expect: A new, empty reservation dialog opens.

steps.say: Enter her name and phone, then set Arrival 28 Oct and Departure 30 Oct.
steps.why: Always enter dates first, because only rooms free on those dates are offered.
steps.expect: Name, phone and the new dates are filled.

steps.say: Click Hold 2 hours.
steps.why: The room is kept for two hours. If nobody confirms it, the hold lapses by itself and shows under Expired.
steps.expect: The booking is saved as Held.

steps.say: Before booking a company guest, the company needs an account with a credit limit, and only the Owner may set a limit. Sagar, the Owner, opens Revenue & Sales, Groups, the Companies tab and clicks New company.
steps.why: A company account lets the hotel bill the company later. Reception asks the Owner for it; reception cannot book a company on credit without one.
steps.expect: The New company account dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the company name Shree Agro Industries, the fictional GSTIN 27AABCS1234A1Z5 and the opening credit limit 50,000 rupees.
steps.why: The credit limit stops the company running up more than the hotel agreed to carry.

steps.say: Click Create account.
steps.why: The company now appears in the booking form and in Accounting as a party.

steps.say: Back at Reception, Aarav books Mr. Vikram Jadhav of Shree Agro Industries: Suite 106 from 24 to 25 October, billed to the company account. Open Reservations, click New reservation and fill the form.
steps.why: The company guest does not pay at check-out; the folio goes to the company account.
steps.expect: The form shows Vikram Jadhav, Suite 106, 24 to 25 October, billed to Shree Agro Industries.

steps.say: Click Confirm reservation.
steps.why: A company booking is confirmed like any other; only the billing differs.
steps.expect: The booking for Vikram Jadhav is confirmed.

steps.say: Press Escape to close the booking dialog.
steps.why: You will check Vikram in later, with the other arrivals.

steps.say: Open the Calendar from Front Desk. Each row is a room and each column a night; coloured bars are bookings.
steps.why: The Calendar shows at a glance which rooms are free on which nights.
steps.expect: The Calendar opens, 24 Oct to 6 Nov.

steps.say: Click Next week to move the window forward a week.
steps.why: The grid shows two weeks at a time; the arrows move it.
steps.expect: The window now starts a week later.

steps.say: Click Today to come back to the business date.
steps.why: Today always returns to 24 Oct 2026, the business date.
steps.expect: The window starts at 24 Oct again.

steps.say: Click an empty cell, for example room 105 from 26 Oct, to start a booking for that room and night.
steps.why: This is the quickest way to book when you are looking at the grid.
steps.expect: The New reservation dialog opens for room 105 from 26 Oct.

steps.say: Press Escape to leave without booking.
steps.why: Nothing is saved until you click Confirm or Hold.

steps.say: Mrs. Kulkarni calls back to cancel. Open Reservations, search booking HCC-1103 and open it.
steps.why: Search by booking number is exact, so you never open the wrong guest.
steps.expect: The booking dialog for the held booking opens.

steps.say: A held booking has Confirm hold when the guest agrees and Cancel hold when she does not. A confirmed booking has Cancel / no-show instead; if money is held on it, refund the advance first.
steps.why: Knowing which button belongs to which status saves a wrong click.
steps.expect: The held booking dialog with Confirm hold and Cancel hold.

steps.say: Click Cancel hold. Mrs. Kulkarni does not want the rooms.
steps.why: A hold is cancelled in two clicks so that nobody cancels one by mistake.
steps.expect: A confirmation asks you to confirm the cancellation.

steps.say: Click Cancel hold again to confirm.
steps.why: Cancelling a hold frees the room at once; the booking stays in the list as Cancelled for the record.
steps.expect: The hold is cancelled and the room is free again.

chapters.title: Arrivals, registration and check-in
chapters.goal: Check in Mr. Rahul Deshmukh with a verified ID and an advance, walk in Ms. Anita Rao, find a guest profile, capture IDs and issue a room key.

steps.say: Rahul Deshmukh has arrived. You are Aarav on Modules Home; check-in starts in the Front Desk module.
steps.why: Check-in is the most important job at the front desk: it ties the guest, the ID and the room together.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile.
steps.why: Arrivals, guests, keys and documents are all front-desk screens.

steps.say: Click the Arrivals & check-in tile.
steps.why: This screen lists everyone expected today.

steps.say: Four bookings are expected today: Ishaan Bose, Vikram Jadhav, Rahul Deshmukh and Aditi Nair. The list shows the registration status, the room status and the advance paid.
steps.why: You see at a glance whether the room is ready and whether the guest is already registered.

steps.say: Type the booking number HCC-1101 in the search box. The box also accepts a name, a room or a vehicle number.
steps.why: A booking number is the surest way to find the right guest.

steps.say: Click Start check-in on Rahul's row.
steps.why: The guided check-in takes you through six steps, so nothing is forgotten.
steps.expect: The guided check-in opens at the registration step.

steps.say: Step 2 of 6 is the registration card. The name and phone come from the booking; address and ID are still empty.
steps.why: The law requires a verified identity for every guest, so the room cannot be given until this step is done.

steps.say: Type the address from the guest's ID: 12 Karve Road, Pune 411004.
steps.why: The address is printed on the registration card and the invoice.

steps.say: Choose the ID type Aadhaar.
steps.why: Each ID type has its own number check; Aadhaar needs exactly twelve digits with a valid check digit.

steps.say: Type the Aadhaar number from the card. The training uses a fictional number that passes the check.
steps.why: After saving, HCC shows the number masked, XXXX XXXX 4321, to everyone except those who may view it.

steps.say: Click Verify registration.
steps.why: The registration is saved and the guest is marked Verified.

steps.say: Room 203 is vacant and ready, so it is eligible. Click Continue.
steps.why: A dirty or blocked room cannot be given; HCC would say why on this step.

steps.say: Read the tariff to the guest, Rs 3,000 a night for 2 nights, and tick that the guest confirmed it.
steps.why: Rate disputes at check-out are avoided when the guest agreed at check-in.

steps.say: Click Continue.
steps.why: Next is the advance. It is optional here.

steps.say: Rahul pays Rs 2,000 as advance. Click Record advance / deposit.
steps.why: An advance is money received before the stay; it is kept on the booking and counted against the final bill.

steps.say: Type the amount 2000.
steps.why: Amounts are entered in rupees and stored exactly.

steps.say: Choose the method UPI.
steps.why: The method decides which cashier total the money joins: cash, UPI, card or bank transfer.

steps.say: Type the UPI reference number from the guest's phone.
steps.why: The reference lets the accountant match the receipt with the bank statement.

steps.say: Click Review.
steps.why: Review shows the balance after posting before anything is saved.
steps.expect: A summary of the receipt is shown.

steps.say: Click Post receipt.
steps.why: Posting a receipt twice is blocked; a repeated click never creates a second receipt.
steps.expect: The receipt is recorded and the booking dialog is shown.

steps.say: Click Guided check-in to continue where you stopped.
steps.why: Completed steps are remembered from the record.

steps.say: Tick the tariff confirmation again and click Continue twice to reach step 6, Check in.
steps.why: The tick belongs to this session; the advance step is complete now.
steps.expect: Step 6 of 6, Check in, with the stay details.

steps.say: Choose the purpose of visit: Business.
steps.why: The purpose of visit is part of the legal guest record.

steps.say: Type the car number MH 12 AB 1234.
steps.why: The vehicle number helps parking and can be searched on this screen.

steps.say: Click Check in.
steps.why: Check-in makes the guest in-house and updates the room board to Occupied.
steps.expect: Rahul Deshmukh is checked in to room 203.
steps.msgText: Checked in to room 203. Room board updated.

steps.say: Click Registration card to see the card the guest signs.
steps.why: The card carries the hotel letterhead, the stay, the guests and the masked ID.

steps.say: This is the registration card of Rahul Deshmukh, with the accompanying guests and the masked ID. Print it, or save a PDF, and let the guest sign.
steps.why: A signed card is the proof of registration.

steps.say: Close the card and the dialog, then open Walk-in on the Arrivals page for a guest without a booking.
steps.why: A walk-in guest is registered and checked in in one step.

steps.say: Ms. Anita Rao from Hyderabad has no booking. Type her name, phone and address.
steps.why: The same registration rules apply to a walk-in.

steps.say: Choose ID type Aadhaar and type her fictional number 345678901238.
steps.why: The ID is checked before the guest can be checked in.

steps.say: Choose room 105, Classic, for one night and the purpose Tourism.
steps.why: Only rooms that are vacant, ready and free for the whole stay are offered.

steps.say: Click Create walk-in and check in.
steps.why: HCC creates the booking, registers the guest and checks her in. Anita pays her bill at the cashier.
steps.expect: Anita Rao is checked in to room 105.

steps.say: Open Guests from Front Desk and search for Deshmukh. This is the guest register.
steps.why: The register keeps one profile per guest, with every stay.
steps.expect: Guests named Rahul Deshmukh are listed.

steps.say: Click Rahul Deshmukh, profile G-1110.
steps.why: The profile shows his contact details, the accompanying guests, photos and the stay history.
steps.expect: The profile opens on the right.

steps.say: Open Document capture under Guests & Services. Here a scanned ID or bill is filed against a guest.
steps.why: Scanning is simulated in the demo; on a real PC the scanner or camera sends the picture here.

steps.say: Key cards are made from the booking. Open the booking of Rahul in Reservations and click Room key.
steps.why: The key belongs to the stay, so it is made from the booking of the stay.
steps.expect: The room key panel opens for room 203 and says the key service is offline.

steps.say: The panel says the encoder is offline. In the training, Meera, the Manager, brings the simulated encoder online on the Room keys page, Encoder tab.
steps.why: Only a manager can switch the encoder. In the real hotel the Key Agent beside the front-desk PC does this by itself.

steps.say: Back at Reception, open the room key panel again and click Issue key to make the card for room 203.
steps.why: The request goes to the encoder at the front desk, which writes the card.
steps.expect: A key request is sent and shown as waiting.

steps.say: At the encoder, the job runs. In the training Meera clicks Finish job on the Encoder tab.
steps.why: When the card is written the job turns to Done and the card is listed under Active cards.

steps.say: Suppose the guest loses the card. Open the room key panel and click Lost card.
steps.why: A lost card is cancelled and a new one issued, so the old card cannot open the door.

steps.say: Click Finish job again on the Encoder tab to write the new card.
steps.why: The old card is cancelled; only the new card opens room 203.

steps.say: Open the Key log tab. It lists every key action with its time, room and user.
steps.why: The log lets the manager see who made which card and when.
steps.expect: The key log shows the issue and the re-issue for room 203.

chapters.title: The Room board
chapters.goal: Read the Room board: status colours, filters, floors, the room drawer, and how a manager blocks and unblocks a room.

steps.say: You are Aarav on Modules Home. The Room board is the screen the front desk looks at most often.
steps.why: It shows every room and its state right now.

steps.say: Click the Front Desk tile.
steps.why: The Room board is the first tile of the module.

steps.say: Click the Room board tile.
steps.why: The board opens on all floors.

steps.say: Every room is a card with its number, type, guest or housekeeping state and the date it is busy until. Rahul Deshmukh is in 203, Anita Rao in 105.
steps.why: You can tell at a glance who is in which room and when they leave.

steps.say: The chips Occupied, Ready, Dirty, Cleaning, Inspection and Blocked filter the board. Ready means clean and sold-ready; Dirty needs cleaning; Inspection waits for the supervisor.
steps.why: Colours always come with a word, so the board is readable without colour.

steps.say: Click the Dirty chip to see only rooms that need cleaning.
steps.why: This is the list housekeeping works from.

steps.say: Click All to see every room again.
steps.why: Always return to All; an old filter hides rooms from the next person.

steps.say: Click Floor 2 to see only the second floor.
steps.why: The floor tabs help on a busy day.

steps.say: Click All floors to see the whole hotel.
steps.why: The tab shows the number of rooms on each floor.

steps.say: Click room 203 to open its drawer.
steps.why: The drawer shows who is in the room and what can be done from here.
steps.expect: The Room 203 drawer opens with the guest Rahul Deshmukh.

steps.say: The drawer lists the guest and the stay, 24 Oct to 26 Oct, and a Report repair button. Reception cannot block a room; that is a manager's decision.
steps.why: A blocked room is removed from sale, so only people responsible for stock may do it.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, opens room 108 on the Room board and clicks Block for repair. Room 108 is dirty and needs a deep clean.
steps.why: A block takes the room out of sale until it is lifted.
steps.expect: The Block for repair form opens.

steps.say: Type the reason: Deep clean.
steps.why: The reason is kept in the room history so everyone knows why the room is off sale.

steps.say: Click Block room.
steps.why: From today the room cannot be booked or given to a guest.

steps.say: When the deep clean is finished, open room 108 again and click Unblock room.
steps.why: Unblocking returns the room to the normal housekeeping flow.
steps.expect: The drawer for 108 shows Change block and Unblock room.

steps.say: Click Unblock room.
steps.why: Housekeeping then cleans and inspects the room as usual.

chapters.title: In-house guests and guest services
chapters.goal: Look after Rahul Deshmukh while he stays: in-house list, requests, wake-up call, a complaint, a room move, reminders and messages.

steps.say: Rahul is in room 203. You are Aarav on Modules Home; everything for guests who are staying lives under Guests & Services.
steps.why: A good stay is made of small requests handled on time.

steps.say: Click the Guests & Services tile.
steps.why: It holds in-house stays, guest requests, messages and document capture.

steps.say: Click the In-house stays tile.
steps.why: This is the list of every guest in the hotel now.

steps.say: The list shows each in-house room with the guest, booking number, stay dates and the balance. Find room 203, Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: The balance column tells reception who still owes money before check-out.

steps.say: Click the row of room 203.
steps.why: The details of the stay open on the right: room segments, occupants and the folio summary.
steps.expect: The details of the stay HCC-1101 open.

steps.say: Click Extend / shorten to see how the departure date is changed.
steps.why: A guest who stays longer or leaves early is handled here, with the folio and the room kept in step.
steps.expect: The Extend / shorten tab shows the departure date.

steps.say: Press Escape. Rahul keeps his dates, so change nothing.
steps.why: The Leaves today tab next to it starts an early check-out.

steps.say: Open Guest services under Guests & Services and click New request. Rahul asks for two extra towels.
steps.why: Every request is logged so that it is done, timed and not forgotten.

steps.say: Choose Room 203, Rahul Deshmukh, and the request Extra towels. Assign it to Ravi.
steps.why: The assignee gets the request on his phone; the priority decides how fast it must be done.
steps.expect: Room 203, Extra towels, assigned to Ravi.

steps.say: Click Log request.
steps.why: The request starts its service clock now.

steps.say: Rahul also wants a wake-up call at 06:30 on 25 October. Click New request, choose Room 203, the request Wake-up call and type the time in Detail.
steps.why: A wake-up request is a promise; the night desk calls at the time given.
steps.expect: A wake-up request for room 203 at 06:30.

steps.say: Click Log request.
steps.why: The wake-up now appears on the Wake-ups list of Reminders & wake-ups.

steps.say: Rahul calls at night: the air conditioner is noisy. Open the Complaints tab.
steps.why: A complaint is different from a request: it needs an owner and a follow-up.

steps.say: Click Log complaint.
steps.why: The dialog links the complaint to the stay.

steps.say: Link it to Room 203, choose the category Maintenance, severity Medium, and describe what happened.
steps.why: The category sends the complaint to the right team; the severity decides how quickly the manager must act.
auto: type:field:What happened|Air conditioner in room 203 is noisy at night

steps.say: Click Log complaint.
steps.why: You will turn this into a work order for the maintenance team later, and offer the guest a service-recovery discount on the folio.

steps.say: Open the Lost & found tab.
steps.why: Anything a guest leaves behind is logged here with the room and the finder; housekeeping adds the entries, reception returns the items.

steps.say: The next day the air conditioner is still faulty, so Rahul is moved. Open In-house stays, open room 203 and click Move room.
steps.why: A move keeps the booking, the folio and the guest history; only the room changes.

steps.say: The dialog offers rooms that are free and ready: 107 Deluxe (same type), 205 Classic and 306 Suite. Room 207 in the plan is reserved for an arrival today, so the training uses 107.
steps.why: Giving the same room type avoids a rate change; a cheaper or dearer type needs the rate rule explained to the guest.

steps.say: Click Move to 107.
steps.why: The old room goes to housekeeping as dirty and the room board changes at once.

steps.say: Ravi, the room attendant, sees the towel request on his phone-style page My guest requests. Open it as Ravi.
steps.why: Housekeepers see only their own requests and no money.
steps.expect: My guest requests lists the towels for room 203.

steps.say: Click Start when you take the request.
steps.why: Start stops the waiting time and starts the work time.

steps.say: Click Complete when the towels are delivered.
steps.why: Completing closes the request and records the service time against the target.

steps.say: Back at Reception, open Reminders & wake-ups under Front Desk and click New reminder.
steps.why: Reminders are notes with a date that the desk sees on the day.

steps.say: Type the subject Collect ID copy from 206, keep today's date and the alert of 3 days.
steps.why: The alert days make the reminder show earlier, so it is not missed.

steps.say: Click Save reminder.
steps.why: The reminder appears on the desk list today and as a banner until it is done.

steps.say: Open the Wake-ups tab.
steps.why: All wake-up calls of the day are listed; the night desk marks each as done after calling.

steps.say: Open Messages under Guests & Services. The Outbox lists every message sent to guests; click Compose.
steps.why: Messages are queued here; sending is simulated in the demo, so no real WhatsApp, SMS or e-mail leaves the hotel.

steps.say: Choose the guest Rahul Deshmukh, the channel WhatsApp and the template Booking confirmation.
steps.why: A template fills the text with the guest's name and booking details.
steps.expect: The message text is filled from the template.

steps.say: Click Queue message.
steps.why: The message waits in the Outbox. A guest who has not given consent receives nothing.
steps.expect: The message is in the Outbox.

steps.say: Click Simulate delivery to play the delivery of the queued messages.
steps.why: In the real hotel the messaging service delivers; here the demo shows what would happen.

steps.say: Open the Consent tab.
steps.why: Guests must agree before they get marketing or service messages; HCC keeps the record.

steps.say: Open the Templates tab.
steps.why: Templates are the standard texts of the hotel; the owner and manager can edit them.
steps.expect: The six message templates are listed.

steps.say: Open the Triggers tab.
steps.why: A trigger is a rule: for example send a welcome message at check-in or a feedback request after check-out.
steps.expect: The seven message rules are listed.

chapters.title: The folio: charges, discounts and corrections
chapters.goal: Open the folio of Rahul Deshmukh, post a laundry charge and a free-text charge, set the meal plan, see how a discount and a rate change go through approval.

steps.say: You are Priya, the cashier, on Modules Home. The folio is the guest's running account: everything the guest owes and has paid.
steps.why: Every rupee a guest pays or owes goes through the folio.

steps.say: Click the Cash & Billing tile.
steps.why: Folios, the cashier shift, the cash book, restaurant checks and expenses are here.

steps.say: Click the Guests & folios tile.
steps.why: This is the list of every guest bill.

steps.say: The chips All, In house, Due out, Balance due, Departed and Confirmed filter the list. Folio requests lists requests waiting for approval.
steps.why: Cashiers use Due out and Balance due to prepare check-outs.

steps.say: Type the booking number HCC-1101.
steps.why: The search also takes a name, a room, a company or an invoice number.
steps.expect: Only the folio of Rahul Deshmukh is listed.

steps.say: Click the folio of Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: The folio opens with his charges, receipts and action buttons.

steps.expect: The Add a service charge dialog opens.

steps.why: Laundry carries GST at 18 per cent, rooms at 5 per cent; HCC takes the rate from the GST master.

steps.say: Click Post charge.
steps.why: The charge joins the folio with CGST and SGST shown separately.
steps.expect: Laundry Rs 500 plus 18 per cent GST is on the folio.

steps.say: Click Add charge again. For something not in the catalogue, choose Other (describe) and type the details.
steps.why: A free-text charge needs a clear description, because it is read later by the accountant and the guest.
steps.expect: The form asks for a description and an amount.

steps.say: Describe it as Courier to Pune and enter the amount 200 rupees.
steps.why: Free-text lines are taxed at 18 per cent as other services.

steps.say: Click Post charge.
steps.why: Both charges are now on the folio.
steps.expect: The courier charge is on the folio.

steps.say: Click Meal plan. Rahul booked bed and breakfast, CP.
steps.why: The plan adds a breakfast line per guest per night.

steps.say: Choose Breakfast included (CP).
steps.why: CP means continental plan: room and breakfast.

steps.say: Click Save plan.
steps.why: The breakfast lines will post with the room nights.

steps.say: Click Rate / guests to see how a rate change is made.
steps.why: A guest rate is never edited silently: the change needs a reason and an approval (rule CTL-01).
steps.expect: The Rate / guest change dialog opens.

steps.say: The dialog shows the rate Rs 3,000, 2 guests, and asks when it applies. A reason is required, and the manager must approve before the new rate counts.
steps.why: Without approval, nobody can lower a rate and pocket the difference.

steps.say: Press Escape. Rahul keeps the agreed rate, so request nothing.
steps.why: Only a request that you submit goes to the manager.

steps.say: Reception offers a service-recovery discount for the noisy air conditioner. Aarav opens Rahul's booking in Reservations and clicks Discount.
steps.why: A discount is a promise of money, so the front desk asks and the manager decides.
steps.expect: The Add a discount dialog opens.

steps.say: Choose the reason Service recovery and type 150 rupees before GST. The rule allows at most 25 per cent of the charges posted so far.
steps.why: The reason is mandatory and appears in the audit and the discount report.

steps.say: Click Submit discount.
steps.why: The discount waits in the manager's approval list; the folio does not change yet.
steps.expect: The discount request is submitted for approval.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, opens Approvals & audit under Admin & Setup. The request waits in the Pending list.
steps.why: The person who asks can never approve their own request.
steps.expect: The Approvals inbox shows one pending request.

steps.say: Click the request to read it: the guest, the booking, the reason and the amount.
steps.why: A manager approves only after reading what exactly is asked.
steps.expect: The request opens with Approve and Reject buttons.

steps.say: Click Approve. Meera agrees to the service-recovery discount.
steps.why: The approval is stamped with the name and time of the manager and written to the audit log; the discount is posted on the folio.
steps.expect: The request is Approved and the discount is posted on the folio.

steps.say: Open Plans & extras under Accounts & Reports. It lists the meal plans and the extra-service catalogue with their prices.
steps.why: The prices you chose from in this chapter come from here; the owner sets them in Masters.

chapters.title: Restaurant and room service
chapters.goal: Open a table check, send the KOT, settle by UPI, void a check, and post a room-service dinner to the room folio.

steps.say: You are Priya on Modules Home. This demo hotel has no separate Restaurant user, so the cashier runs the restaurant checks.
steps.why: Restaurant sales, like every other sale, are part of the same day's cash and tax figures.

steps.say: Click the Cash & Billing tile.
steps.why: The restaurant screen sits next to the folios and the cash book.

steps.say: Click the Restaurant & room service tile.
steps.why: One screen handles tables and room service.

steps.say: The Orders tab shows tables T1 to T8 and the open and settled checks of the day. The Kitchen (KOT) tab lists orders sent to the kitchen, and Day summary totals the day. Restaurant and Room service switch between table and room checks.
steps.why: The cashier sees the whole outlet on one page.
steps.expect: The restaurant page with the eight tables.

steps.say: Click the free table T4.
steps.why: A table that is free shows Tap to open a check.
steps.expect: The Open a check dialog opens for Table T4.

steps.say: Type a reference for the check: Rahul Deshmukh guests. Covers is 2.
steps.why: The reference helps the waiter and the cashier find the check later.

steps.say: Click Open check.
steps.why: An open check collects dishes until the guest asks for the bill.
steps.expect: The check for Table T4 is open.

steps.say: Click the Breakfast chip to show the breakfast dishes.
steps.why: The chips group the menu: Beverages, Breakfast, Starters, Mains, Breads & rice, Desserts.

steps.say: Click Add Masala dosa, Rs 220.
steps.why: Each click adds one portion to the check.
steps.expect: One Masala dosa is on the check.

steps.say: Click Increase on the Masala dosa line to make it two.
steps.why: Plus and minus buttons change the quantity without adding a new line.
steps.expect: Two Masala dosa are on the check.

steps.say: Click the Beverages chip.
steps.why: Drinks are on a separate chip.

steps.say: Click Add Masala chai, Rs 60, twice for two cups.
steps.why: The check keeps one line per dish with the quantity.
steps.expect: Masala chai is on the check.

steps.say: Click Send KOT.
steps.why: The kitchen order ticket tells the kitchen what to cook. Items are fixed after the KOT; changes later go through a void.
steps.expect: The KOT is sent to the kitchen.

steps.say: Open the Kitchen (KOT) tab.
steps.why: The kitchen sees each ticket with its table and items, and marks them Preparing and Ready.
steps.expect: The KOT list opens with the ticket for Table T4.

steps.say: Go back to Orders and open the check of Table T4.
steps.why: The cashier works from the Orders tab.
steps.expect: The T4 check is shown with the Settle button.

steps.say: Click Settle. The guests ask for the bill.
steps.why: Settling closes the check, issues the bill number and records the payment.

steps.say: Choose UPI as the payment method.
steps.why: Cash, UPI, card and room folio are the four ways; each joins its own cashier total.

steps.say: Type the UPI reference shown on the phone of the guest.
steps.why: The reference is needed for UPI and card payments so the accountant can match the bank statement.

steps.say: Click the Settle button with the amount.
steps.why: The bill carries 5 per cent GST for the restaurant, split into CGST and SGST, and gets the next number of the POS series.
steps.expect: The check is settled and a bill number is issued.

steps.say: Another table, T5: a guest orders a dosa and then leaves. Open T5, add a Masala dosa and send the KOT.
steps.why: Sometimes a check must be cancelled; that is what Void bill is for.
steps.expect: The T5 check shows Void bill.

steps.say: Click Void bill.
steps.why: A void needs a written reason and is kept in the audit log with the user and the time.
steps.expect: The Void the whole bill dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the reason: Guest left before the food came.
steps.why: A clear reason lets the manager check the void in the day report.
steps.value: Guest left before the food came
auto: type:field:Reason|Guest left before the food came

steps.say: Click Void now.
steps.why: The check disappears from the open list but not from the records.

steps.say: Now room service. Click Room service and open the check of room 107, where Rahul Deshmukh stays.
steps.why: A room-service check is charged to the room, not paid at the table.
steps.expect: The rooms with guests are listed.

steps.say: Click Room 107, open the check and add Aloo paratha with curd, Jeera rice and two Butter naan.
steps.why: The dishes are the guest's dinner order.
steps.expect: The room-service check has four lines.

steps.say: Click Send KOT.
steps.why: The kitchen cooks and the order goes up to the room.

steps.say: Click Settle.
steps.why: For a room guest the payment method is Room folio.

steps.say: Choose Room folio.
steps.why: The amount is posted to the guest's folio and paid at check-out with everything else.

steps.say: Click Post to room folio.
steps.why: The dinner is posted to the folio of room 107 with 5 per cent GST.
steps.expect: The dinner is on the folio of Rahul Deshmukh.

steps.say: Open the Day summary tab.
steps.why: It totals the day's restaurant sales by payment method, and shows the bill and KOT numbers issued.

chapters.title: Cashier: shift, payments, cash book
chapters.goal: Read the cashier shift, count the drawer, see the bank deposit and till transfer forms, take Ms. Anita Rao's cash payment and read the cash book.

steps.say: You are Priya on Modules Home. The cashier works from the Cashier shift screen: it knows how much cash should be in the drawer.
steps.why: The cashier answers for every rupee in the drawer, so the screen counts for you and asks you to count back.

steps.say: Click the Cash & Billing tile.
steps.why: The cashier shift is the second tile after the folios.

steps.say: Click the Cashier shift tile.
steps.why: There is one cash shift per business day.

steps.say: Step 1 says the shift is Open: the expected cash is Rs 10,725 and the opening float carried from the last counted close is Rs 5,000. The five steps on the left take you from the expected cash to the credit guests.
steps.why: The float is carried from yesterday's counted close, so a shortage is never hidden in the opening.

steps.say: Click 3. Cash movements to see what moved through the drawer today.
steps.why: Every receipt, refund, restaurant cash bill, deposit and expense in cash is listed.
steps.expect: The cash movements of the day are listed.

steps.say: Click 2. Count & result.
steps.why: At the end of the shift the cashier counts the cash and enters the total.

steps.say: Type a count to see what happens: 10700.
steps.why: HCC shows the difference at once, so the cashier can recount before closing.
steps.expect: The Difference box shows the shortage of Rs 25.

steps.say: Click Denominations to count note by note.
steps.why: Counting by notes helps when the total does not match.
steps.expect: One box per note value appears.

steps.say: Click Bank deposit.
steps.why: When cash is taken to the bank, the cashier records it here with the slip.

steps.say: The form asks for the amount, the bank and account, the deposit-slip number and a photo of the slip. The photo is required, so a deposit cannot be recorded without proof.
steps.why: The manager and the accountant can open the slip photo later.

steps.say: Press Escape; no deposit is made in the training.
steps.why: Nothing is saved until you click Record bank deposit.

steps.say: Click Till transfer.
steps.why: Cash can move between the front-desk drawer and the back-office cash, for example to give change.

steps.say: Press Escape.
steps.why: A till transfer has an amount and a reason, and both tills record it.

steps.say: Anita Rao pays her bill now, in cash. Open Guests & folios, search HCC-1115 and open her folio.
steps.why: Cash is taken at the cashier, never by the room attendant.
steps.expect: The folio of Ms. Anita Rao opens.

steps.say: Click Record payment.
steps.why: A payment before check-out is an advance against the final bill.

steps.say: Type 2100: one night at Rs 2,000 plus 5 per cent GST.
steps.why: The cashier takes the whole amount; any difference is settled at check-out.

steps.say: Click Review.
steps.why: Review shows the balance after posting.
steps.expect: The summary of the receipt is shown.

steps.say: Click Post receipt.
steps.why: The cash receipt is added to the drawer total at once.

steps.say: Open the Cash book under Cash & Billing. It shows the day's cash and bank money by account.
steps.why: The cash book is the daily record the accountant checks against the bank.
steps.expect: The Cash book opens with the drawer and the hotel current account.

steps.say: Each block lists the receipts and payments of one account: the front-desk cash drawer, the hotel current account and money not settled through an account. CSV and Excel buttons export the day.
steps.why: The book follows the same numbers as the cashier shift and the day close.

chapters.title: Check-out, invoice, credit note, counter bills
chapters.goal: Check out Ms. Anita Rao and the company guest Mr. Vikram Jadhav, take the card payment of Mr. Rahul Deshmukh, check him out, read the GST invoice and issue a counter bill.

steps.say: It is now 25 October. The night audit and the day close ran at the end of 24 October (chapter 19 shows them in detail), so room nights are posted and Anita Rao and Vikram Jadhav are due out.
steps.why: A guest can only be checked out once every agreed room night is posted by the night audit.

steps.say: The wake-up call of the guest and the reminder from chapter 4 are due. Meera, the Manager, clicks Done on both banners at the top.
steps.why: A banner stays on every screen until somebody marks it Done, so nobody forgets a call.

steps.say: Aarav opens the booking of Ms. Anita Rao, HCC-1115, from Reservations. She paid Rs 2,100 in cash, so the balance is zero.
steps.why: Check-out starts from the booking dialog.
steps.expect: The booking dialog of Anita Rao opens.

steps.say: Click Checkout.
steps.why: The dialog reviews the folio before the room is released.
steps.expect: The Ready to say goodbye? dialog opens.

steps.say: The dialog shows the room nights posted against agreed, the total charges, the payments, the balance, the deposit to return and any pending approvals. It is blocked while anything is open. For Anita everything is clear.
steps.why: Check-out cannot finish while there is a balance, a deposit or an approval waiting.
steps.expect: The check-out review for Anita Rao.

steps.say: Click Confirm checkout.
steps.why: The room goes to housekeeping as dirty and the invoice number is allocated once.

steps.say: Click the invoice button.
steps.why: The invoice is created at check-out and cannot be created again.

steps.say: The tax invoice shows the guest, the invoice number, and every line with its GST rate, CGST and SGST. In this demo it is stamped as a sample, and the number series is DEMO.
steps.why: Rooms up to Rs 7,500 a night carry 5 per cent GST; other services 18 per cent; CGST and SGST are always equal halves.
steps.expect: The tax invoice of Anita Rao.

steps.say: Mr. Vikram Jadhav of Shree Agro Industries is due out. Open his booking HCC-1107 and click Checkout.
steps.why: A company guest does not pay at the desk.
steps.expect: The check-out review shows a balance of Rs 4,725 and the company credit box.

steps.say: The review shows the balance Rs 4,725 and a box Company credit, Shree Agro Industries: Rs 4,725 used of Rs 50,000, Rs 45,275 left. The balance moves to the company's receivable, and needs approval: a Manager up to Rs 10,000, the Owner above.
steps.why: The credit limit and the approval protect the hotel from unpaid company bills.

steps.say: Click Request company credit for Rs 4,725.
steps.why: The request goes to the manager; the guest need not wait at the desk.
steps.expect: The request is sent for approval.

steps.say: Meera opens Approvals & audit, clicks the request of Vikram Jadhav and reads it.
steps.why: The manager sees the amount and the company before agreeing.
steps.expect: The request opens with Approve and Reject.

steps.say: Click Approve.
steps.why: The amount is now a receivable of Shree Agro Industries and appears in Accounting.

steps.say: Aarav opens the booking again and clicks Checkout.
steps.why: With the approval in place the check-out is no longer blocked.
steps.expect: The review shows the balance moved to the company.

steps.say: Click Confirm checkout.
steps.why: The guest leaves; the company account owes Rs 4,725.

steps.say: Next morning, 26 October, Rahul Deshmukh leaves. The night audit of 25 October has run.
steps.why: Both room nights of his stay are now posted.

steps.say: Priya opens Guests & folios, searches HCC-1101 and opens the folio of Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: The folio shows what he owes after all charges.
steps.expect: The folio of Rahul Deshmukh opens.

steps.say: The folio lists the room nights at 5 per cent, the laundry and courier at 18 per cent, the approved service-recovery discount, the room-service dinner and the breakfast plan. The advance of Rs 2,000 is deducted. The balance is what Rahul pays now.
steps.why: Always read the balance to the guest before taking the money.
steps.expect: The final folio with the balance.

steps.say: Click Record payment for the balance.
steps.why: The balance is paid by card, so the receipt carries the card reference.

steps.say: Choose Card.
steps.why: The method decides the cashier total the money joins.

steps.say: The amount field takes the whole balance of the folio. Type it exactly as the folio shows it.
steps.why: Paying the exact balance leaves nothing to settle later.

steps.say: Type the card slip reference.
steps.why: The reference lets the accountant match the card settlement.

steps.say: Click Review.
steps.why: Review shows that the balance after posting is zero.
steps.expect: The receipt summary shows a zero balance.

steps.say: Click Post receipt.
steps.why: The folio is now fully paid.

steps.say: Aarav opens the booking and clicks Checkout. Nothing blocks it now.
steps.why: Reception releases the room.
steps.expect: The review shows a zero balance.

steps.say: Click Confirm checkout.
steps.why: Room 107 goes to housekeeping.
steps.expect: Rahul Deshmukh is checked out and the invoice is allocated.

steps.say: Click the invoice button.
steps.why: The invoice sums every line with the GST rate that applied on the day.

steps.say: Rooms and food at 5 per cent, laundry and courier at 18 per cent, the discount as a negative line. Print or save it as a PDF for the guest. A duplicate is printed from the same screen and is marked as a duplicate.
steps.why: The guest takes the invoice with him; the same number is never issued twice.

steps.say: Click Back to folio.
steps.why: The folio of a departed guest stays open for corrections.
steps.expect: The folio of the departed guest is shown.

steps.say: Click Request credit note. Suppose the guest was charged Rs 100 too much.
steps.why: After the invoice is issued only a credit note can reduce it, and only the Owner approves it.

steps.say: Type the credit amount 100 before GST and the reason: Courier charged twice.
steps.why: The reason goes on the credit note and into the audit log.

steps.say: Click Submit credit note request.
steps.why: The request waits for the Owner; the invoice does not change yet.
steps.expect: The credit note request is submitted.

steps.say: Sagar, the Owner, opens Approvals & audit and opens the request.
steps.why: Only the Owner can approve a credit note.
steps.expect: The credit note request opens with Approve and Reject.

steps.say: Click Approve.
steps.why: The credit note is issued with its own number against the invoice.

steps.say: Now a counter bill. Open Counter bills under Cash & Billing. Anita Rao's friend wants to pay for a lunch.
steps.why: A counter bill is for people who are not staying in the hotel.
steps.expect: The Counter bills page opens on New bill.

steps.say: Type the customer Mr. Sanjay Rao, choose Free text, describe the item as Lunch for two at 600 rupees with the GST type food.
steps.why: Food is taxed at 5 per cent, laundry at 18 per cent; the GST type decides the rate.

steps.say: Click Add line.
steps.why: A bill can have many lines; each keeps its own GST rate.
steps.expect: The line is added to the bill.

steps.say: Settlement is Paid now, by cash. Click Issue counter bill.
steps.why: The bill gets its own number and the cash joins the drawer total at once.

steps.say: Open the Bills tab to see the bills issued. Choose Udhaar credit when the customer will pay later.
steps.why: Udhaar is credit given to a customer; it is a receivable until the customer pays and appears in the cashier shift and the accounts.
steps.expect: The list of counter bills opens.

steps.say: Open Approvals & audit under Admin & Setup to see all requests in one place.
steps.why: Approvals are how managers and owners keep control without standing at the desk.
steps.expect: The Approvals inbox opens with the tabs Pending, Approved, Rejected, Expired, Invalidated and Executed.

steps.say: Open the Audit log tab.
steps.why: Every approval, void and credit note leaves a line with the user and the time; the log cannot be edited.

chapters.title: Housekeeping
chapters.goal: Run the housekeeping board: tasks, assigning, cleaning with the checklist, inspection, reporting a repair and logging a found item. No hotel money is shown to housekeeping.

steps.say: It is 26 October. Neha, the housekeeping supervisor, starts on Modules Home. She has no Front Desk or Cash & Billing tile, only the modules her work needs.
steps.why: Housekeeping and maintenance staff never see the hotel's money (rule DEC-061).
steps.expect: Modules Home for Neha: Housekeeping & Maintenance, Guests & Services, Revenue & Sales, Stock & Purchasing, People & Payroll, Admin & Setup.

steps.say: Click the Housekeeping & Maintenance tile.
steps.why: The board, work orders and the shift handover are in this module.

steps.say: Click the Housekeeping tile.
steps.why: This is the board the whole housekeeping team works from.

steps.say: The board has four columns: To do, In progress, Awaiting inspection and Done, and a panel showing each attendant's load. Each card is a room with its task, zone, standard minutes and assignee. There is no price or amount anywhere.
steps.why: The load panel tells the supervisor who has too many rooms.
steps.expect: The board with the task columns.

steps.say: Use the Assignee filter and choose Ravi.
steps.why: A supervisor can look at one attendant's work at a time.

steps.say: Choose Everyone again.
steps.why: Return filters to the full view before you leave the screen.

steps.say: Room 203 was left by Rahul Deshmukh and sits in the To do column. Every card has an assignee drop-down; the supervisor can give the room to another attendant there.
steps.why: Moving a task balances the day without telling anyone twice.
steps.expect: Room 203 is in the To do column.

steps.say: Ravi, the room attendant, opens the same page on his own login. He opens Housekeeping, finds room 203 and clicks Start cleaning.
steps.why: Starting a task starts its timer; attendants see only their own tasks.
steps.expect: Room 203 moves to In progress with a three-item checklist.

steps.say: Tick the three checklist items: Linen & bathroom, Surfaces & amenities and Final room check.
steps.why: Complete cleaning stays grey until every item is ticked, so no step is skipped.

steps.say: Click Complete cleaning.

steps.say: Neha opens the board again. Room 203 and room 303 wait for inspection. Click Inspect & release on room 203.
steps.why: An inspection by a second person is what makes a room Ready.

steps.say: Click Inspect & release.
steps.why: The room becomes Ready and appears as available on the Room board and in new reservations.
steps.expect: Room 203 is Ready and leaves the board.

steps.say: For room 303 the supervisor finds a stain and clicks Return for cleaning.
steps.why: A failed inspection sends the room back to the attendant; it stays unsellable.

steps.say: Describe the problem and send it back. In the training Neha writes: Bathroom floor not clean.
steps.why: The reason tells the attendant what to fix.

steps.say: Click the button that returns the room.
steps.why: The task goes back to To do for the same attendant.
steps.expect: Room 303 is back in To do.

steps.say: On the card of room 107 click Report repair. Rahul reported the air conditioner of the room he left as noisy.
steps.why: Housekeeping sees faults first; reporting them starts the maintenance work.
steps.expect: The Report a repair dialog opens.

steps.say: Describe the fault: Air conditioner noisy, compressor rattle.
steps.why: The maintenance team reads this text, so be specific.
auto: type:field:What needs repair|Air conditioner noisy, compressor rattle

steps.say: Click Report repair.
steps.why: A repair request is created for Maintenance; chapter 10 follows it up.

steps.say: Click Room details on any card, for example room 105, to see its drawer.
steps.why: From the drawer a supervisor can also block the room for repair.
steps.expect: The room 105 drawer opens with Report repair and Block for repair.

steps.say: Close the drawer. Ravi found a phone charger in room 105 after Ms. Anita Rao left. He opens Guests & Services, My guest requests and clicks Log found item.
steps.why: Everything found is logged with the room and where it is kept.
steps.expect: The Log a found item dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the item Phone charger, choose the category Electronics, the room 105 and the storage Front office safe.
steps.why: Reception returns found items from the register and matches them with a guest.

steps.say: Click Log item.
steps.why: The item is on the Lost & found list for reception.

steps.say: Back as Aarav at Reception, open Guest services, the Lost & found tab, to see the item and the complaints list.
steps.why: Reception does the returns and answers the complaints.
steps.expect: The Lost & found list shows the phone charger.

steps.say: Open the Complaints tab to see the air-conditioner complaint of chapter 4.
steps.why: A complaint stays open until it is resolved and the guest has been answered.

chapters.title: Maintenance
chapters.goal: Follow a repair from the housekeeping request to a closed work order, book a spare part, and see the manager's view: preventive plans, assets, spares, vendors and AMC. Money stays hidden from the maintenance team.

steps.say: Joseph is the maintenance technician. On Modules Home he has the Housekeeping & Maintenance module; like housekeeping he sees no hotel money.
steps.why: Maintenance staff work on faults and parts, not on prices.

steps.say: Click the Housekeeping & Maintenance tile.
steps.why: Housekeeping, Maintenance and Checklists & handover are the three screens.
steps.expect: The module page opens with three tiles.

steps.say: Click the Maintenance tile.
steps.why: For a technician the page is called My work orders.

steps.say: The page lists Joseph's open work orders, and below them the repair requests that housekeeping has reported for him. The request Room 107, Air conditioner noisy, compressor rattle came from the housekeeping board in chapter 9.
steps.why: A request is only a report; a work order is the tracked job with a priority, a time target and parts.
steps.expect: My work orders and the repair requests.

steps.say: Click Create work order on the request for room 107.
steps.why: The work order gets a number, a priority and a service-level clock from the moment it exists.
steps.expect: The work order is created from the request.
steps.msgText: Work order created from the repair request

steps.say: Click Start work on the new work order.
steps.why: Starting tells the front desk that somebody is on the job, and moves the clock from waiting to working.
steps.expect: The work order is In progress.

steps.say: Click Add part to book a spare used on the job.
steps.why: Parts are booked against the work order so stock and cost stay right.
steps.expect: The Add part used dialog opens.

steps.say: Choose the spare from the list and the quantity. Joseph sees the part names and the stock left, but never the price.
steps.why: The accountant sees the cost in the reports; the technician does not need it.

steps.say: Choose the first spare in the list and book one piece.
steps.why: Booking reduces the spares stock at once.
steps.expect: The spare is selected with quantity 1.

steps.say: Click Book part.
steps.why: The part is listed on the work order.

steps.say: Click Complete when the repair is done.
steps.why: A complete work order is closed with a note, never silently.

steps.say: Write what you did: Tightened compressor mount and replaced the filter mesh. Noise gone.
steps.why: The note is the history of the room's air conditioner for the next technician.
steps.value: Tightened compressor mount and replaced the filter mesh. Noise gone.
auto: type:field:What did you do|Tightened compressor mount and replaced the filter mesh. Noise gone.

steps.say: Click Mark complete.
steps.why: The work order moves to Done, awaiting the supervisor's check.
steps.expect: The work order is complete and waits for a check.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, opens Maintenance. She sees every work order, the repair requests and six tabs.
steps.why: The manager watches priorities and the service-level times of the whole hotel.
steps.expect: The manager's Maintenance page opens on Work orders.

steps.say: Open the Preventive tab.
steps.why: A preventive plan, for example Geyser service, creates work orders on a schedule so that machines are serviced before they fail.
steps.expect: The PM schedule lists the plans.

steps.say: Open the Assets tab.
steps.why: Every machine of the hotel has a record: air conditioners, geysers, the lift and the fire pump, each with its room.

steps.say: Open the Spares tab.
steps.why: Spares show what is in stock and when to reorder.

steps.say: Open the Vendors & AMC tab.
steps.why: Annual maintenance contracts show which contractor services which machine and until when.
steps.expect: Vendors and AMC contracts are listed.

steps.say: Open the Reports tab.
steps.why: The reports show work orders by status, repeat faults and room downtime.

chapters.title: Checklists and handover
chapters.goal: Complete the housekeeping shift checklist, submit it, and write the handover note for the next shift.

steps.say: Neha is at the end of the morning shift. On Modules Home she opens the Housekeeping & Maintenance module.
steps.why: A shift is not over until its checklist is done and its handover is written.

steps.say: Click the Housekeeping & Maintenance tile.
steps.why: The checklists are the third tile.

steps.say: Click the Checklists & handover tile.
steps.why: It keeps the checklists of the current shift and the notes between shifts.
steps.expect: The page opens on My checklists.

steps.say: My checklists shows the current shift, Morning 07:00 to 15:00, and two checklists: 1. Housekeeping floor check and 2. Maintenance rounds, each with its percentage done.
steps.why: The percentage tells the manager how far the shift has got.
steps.expect: Two checklists for the morning shift.

steps.say: Tick each item of the Housekeeping floor check: the trolley is stocked, corridors are clean, found items are logged, the Do-Not-Disturb rooms are noted, linen is checked, repairs are reported and chemicals are locked.
steps.why: Each tick is a statement that the thing was really checked.
steps.expect: All seven items are ticked, the corridor item carries a simulated photo, and the checklist shows 100 per cent.

steps.say: Click Submit checklist.
steps.why: A submitted checklist cannot be changed and is visible to the manager.

steps.say: Open the Handover tab.
steps.why: Handover notes are what one shift tells the next: open issues, keys and guest notes.

steps.say: Click Write handover note.
steps.why: The outgoing supervisor writes it before leaving.
steps.expect: The Write handover note dialog opens.

steps.say: Choose the desk Housekeeping and the outgoing shift Morning. Untick Nothing to report and type the open issue: Room 107 air conditioner repaired, check it at the inspection.
steps.why: A note that says nothing to report is also a statement, so it is a tick box.
auto: type:field:Open issues|Room 107 air conditioner repaired, check it at the inspection

steps.say: Click Submit handover.
steps.why: The next shift sees the note when it opens the screen and marks it done.

steps.say: The Housekeeping handover of the morning shift is now at the top of the list, with Mark done for the evening shift to click after reading it. The filters All, Housekeeping and Maintenance narrow the list.
steps.why: Reading and marking done closes the loop between shifts.
steps.expect: The handover list with the new note.

chapters.title: Customers 360
chapters.goal: Find a customer, read the whole history on one screen, see who viewed an ID, and keep preferences and notes on the profile.

steps.say: You are Aarav on Modules Home. The Customers tile opens the page of customer profiles; with only one page in the module, the tile goes straight to it.
steps.why: Customers 360 is the memory of the hotel: every stay, payment and request of one person.

steps.say: Click the Customers tile.
steps.why: The page keeps one profile per person, built from all stays.
steps.expect: The Customers page opens with the list on the left.

steps.say: The list shows each customer with the mobile number, the number of stays and the last stay. Badges say In house or Repeat; stays marked legacy come from the old Lodge software.
steps.why: A returning guest can be greeted by name and given the room he liked.

steps.say: Type the mobile number 9800000001 in the search box.
steps.why: Search takes a name, a mobile number or a vehicle number.

steps.say: Click Rahul Deshmukh.
steps.why: His profile opens on the right.
steps.expect: The profile opens on the Overview tab.

steps.say: The Overview tab shows the contact details, the accompanying guest Mrs. Sneha Deshmukh, photos and the stay history. The tabs Stays, Legacy, Money and Notes & requests hold the detail.
steps.why: Everything you need to talk to the guest is on one screen.

steps.say: Open the Stays tab.
steps.why: Each stay shows the dates, rooms and booking number; a room move appears as 203 then 107.

steps.say: Open the Legacy tab.
steps.why: Stays imported from the old Lodge software appear here; a new guest has none.
steps.expect: The legacy list is empty for Rahul.

steps.say: Open the Money tab.
steps.why: The bills of the guest are listed with their totals.
steps.expect: The bill of the stay is listed.

steps.say: Open the Notes & requests tab.
steps.why: Guest requests such as the towels and the wake-up call, with their status, are kept on the profile.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, opens the profile and clicks Show ID. The ID can only be seen by roles that may.
steps.why: Seeing an ID is a privacy event, so HCC logs every view.
steps.expect: The ID is shown and the view is logged.
steps.msgText: ID shown — this view is logged

steps.say: Click Edit profile to keep preferences and notes.
steps.why: Preferences and notes travel with the guest to every future stay.

steps.say: Click Edit profile inside the dialog.
steps.why: The form opens with the saved values.
steps.expect: The Edit Rahul Deshmukh form opens.

steps.say: Type the preferences: Quiet room, away from the lift, and the note: Business traveller, wants a GST invoice.
steps.why: A good preference saves a complaint next time.
auto: type:field:Preferences|Quiet room, away from the lift
type:field:Notes|Business traveller, wants a GST invoice

steps.say: Click Save profile.
steps.why: The profile is saved and the next booking shows the preferences.

steps.say: Open the Foreigner register tab.
steps.why: Hotels must report foreign guests; this register lists them for a date range and prints the form.
steps.expect: The register opens for the last month.

steps.say: Open Guests under Front Desk. Profiles that look the same are flagged Possible duplicate; HCC never merges records by itself.
steps.why: A person with two profiles splits their history; the flag lets reception clean it up.
steps.expect: Two Aarav Joshi profiles are listed with the flag.

chapters.title: Tariff, yield and the tariff card
chapters.goal: Read the rate calendar and the pricing rules, send a rate change for approval, approve it as Owner, and prepare and print a tariff card.

steps.say: Meera, the Manager, is on Modules Home. Prices are set in the Revenue & Sales module.
steps.why: The manager proposes price changes; the Owner decides.

steps.say: Click the Revenue & Sales tile.
steps.why: Tariff, groups, OTA, the booking site and the halls are here.

steps.say: Click the Tariff & yield tile.
steps.why: It shows the live rate and the rate HCC suggests for every night.
steps.expect: Tariff & yield opens on the Rate calendar.

steps.say: The Rate calendar lists each room type and night with the suggested rate and the live rate. For Classic on Saturday 31 Oct HCC suggests Rs 2,400 while the live rate is still Rs 2,000.
steps.why: Suggestions come from the season, the day of the week and how full the hotel is; nothing changes until a publish is approved.

steps.say: Open the Rate plans tab.
steps.why: It holds the rate sheet and a calculator that quotes a stay.
steps.expect: The rate sheet and the quote form open.

steps.say: Open the Rules tab.
steps.why: Seasons, days of the week, occupancy tiers and guardrails are the rules behind the suggestions; the guardrails stop a rate going too low or too high.

steps.say: Open the Restrictions tab.
steps.why: A restriction, such as a minimum stay on a festival weekend, protects the best nights.

steps.say: Open the History tab.
steps.why: Every published change is kept with its reason and who approved it.
steps.expect: The history of rate changes opens.

steps.say: Click Propose publish to send the suggested rates for approval.
steps.why: A manager cannot change the live price alone.
steps.expect: The Propose a tariff publish dialog opens.

steps.say: Choose the first and last night and the room types, and give a reason that is kept in the history and shown to the approver.
steps.why: A clear reason makes the Owner's decision quick.

steps.say: Type the reason: Weekend uplift for the festival days.
steps.why: The reason is shown to the Owner.
steps.value: Weekend uplift for the festival days
auto: type:field:Reason|Weekend uplift for the festival days

steps.say: Click Send for approval.
steps.why: The request waits for the Owner; the live rates stay as they are.

steps.say: Sagar, the Owner, opens Tariff & yield. A new tab, Publish requests, shows the request. Open it.
steps.why: Only the Owner publishes prices.
steps.expect: The publish request is listed with Approve & publish and Reject.

steps.say: Click Approve & publish.
steps.why: From that night on the new rates are live for new bookings; existing bookings keep their agreed rate.

steps.say: Now the tariff card. Back as Meera, open Tariff card under Revenue & Sales and click New draft.
steps.why: The tariff card is the printed price list of rooms, meal plans, extras and halls, valid from a date.
steps.expect: A draft card TRC-0001 opens with every price including GST.

steps.say: The draft lists every room type, extra person, extra bed, meal plan and hall with the price including GST. The tabs Rooms, Meal plans & extras, Seasons & weekends and Halls hold the groups.
steps.why: Guests ask for the card at the desk; it must always match the live prices.

steps.say: Open the Seasons & weekends tab.
steps.why: Season uplifts are printed on the card so that guests know the weekend rate.

steps.say: The Propose button sends the draft to the Owner, who publishes it. The training does not send it, because a card with the same start date as the rates just published would be refused.
steps.why: Two price lists for the same date would confuse the desk, so HCC refuses the second.

steps.say: Open the Print tab.
steps.why: The card prints on one page with the hotel name and the valid-from date; printing never changes a price.
steps.expect: The print preview of the tariff card opens.

chapters.title: Groups, companies, OTA and website
chapters.goal: Block six rooms for the Patil wedding, read company accounts and credit limits, handle booking requests from an OTA, and read the direct booking site.

steps.say: Meera is on Modules Home. Group blocks, companies, OTA channels and the booking website are all sales functions of the Revenue & Sales module.
steps.why: Selling rooms in bulk is the manager's work.

steps.say: Click the Revenue & Sales tile.
steps.why: The sales screens are listed as tiles.

steps.say: Click the Groups & corporate tile.
steps.why: Blocks, companies, pickup and limit requests are on one page.

steps.say: The figures at the top show the open blocks, the rooms picked up against held, the unpicked rooms and the credit alerts. The tabs are Blocks, Companies, Pickup report, Master folio and Limit requests.
steps.why: A block that is not picked up before its cut-off date should be released to the public.
steps.expect: The groups page with its tabs.

steps.say: Click New group block for the Patil wedding.
steps.why: A block holds rooms for a group without naming the guests yet.
steps.expect: The New group block dialog opens.

steps.say: Type the group name Patil wedding block, arrival 30 Oct, departure 1 Nov and the cut-off 28 Oct.
steps.why: The cut-off is the last day the group may name its guests; after it the unpicked rooms return to sale.
steps.expect: The name and the dates are filled.

steps.say: Hold 2 Classic, 3 Deluxe and 1 Suite, six rooms in all, with the contact Mr. Anil Patil.
steps.why: The rate per type comes from the tariff and can be changed for a group.

steps.say: Click Create block.
steps.why: The six rooms are taken out of general sale.

steps.say: Open the Blocks tab and click the Patil wedding block.
steps.why: The detail shows each room type: held, picked up, released, remaining and free now.
steps.expect: The block detail opens with the Rooming list, Allotment, Release and Cancel block buttons.

steps.say: Click Rooming list.
steps.why: The rooming list is where each held room gets a guest name and becomes a booking.

steps.say: Press Escape. The wedding party will send its names later.
steps.why: Unpicked rooms stay held until the cut-off date.

steps.say: Open the Companies tab.
steps.why: Each company account shows its credit limit and its balance.

steps.say: Click Credit limit on Shree Agro Industries.
steps.why: A manager can request a change of limit; the Owner decides.

steps.say: Press Escape; the limit stays Rs 50,000.
steps.why: Requests appear on the Limit requests tab for the Owner.

steps.say: Open the Master folio tab.
steps.why: A master folio collects the charges of a whole group on one bill.

steps.say: Open the Pickup report tab.
steps.why: The report shows how many held rooms each block has picked up.

steps.say: Open OTA channels under Revenue & Sales. OTA means online travel agent, such as TripKart, BookNest and StayHub.
steps.why: Bookings from agents arrive in an inbox and are accepted or rejected here.
steps.expect: The OTA channels page opens on the Inbox.

steps.say: The Inbox lists new bookings and changes from each channel, with Accept and Reject. Accepting a booking creates a normal reservation with the channel as source and the commission recorded.
steps.why: An unanswered booking may be lost to another hotel, so the inbox is checked often.

steps.say: The Pre-check column says whether a booking can be accepted: BookNest BN-88231 for Kiran Joshi, Deluxe, 27 to 29 Oct, shows Can accept, Room 103. Others show Cannot accept, for example when the arrival date is already past or the party is too big for the room.
steps.why: HCC checks the room, the date and the capacity before you accept.

steps.say: Click Accept on the BookNest booking BN-88231.
steps.why: The reservation is created and the room is blocked for the guest of the agent.
steps.expect: The booking is accepted and appears in Reservations.

steps.say: Open the Commission report tab.
steps.why: The commission the hotel owes each agent is worked out from the accepted bookings.

steps.say: Open the Payouts tab.
steps.why: Payouts are the payments of the agent to the hotel after the commission; the accountant records them.

steps.say: Open Direct booking site under Revenue & Sales. Guests who book on the website of the hotel arrive here as web booking requests.
steps.why: Direct bookings carry no commission, so they are the most valuable.
steps.expect: The Direct booking site page opens on Bookings.

steps.say: Open the Preview tab.
steps.why: The preview shows the page guests see on the website, including the QR code that opens the feedback form.
steps.expect: The preview of the booking page opens.
